Subject: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency SLOs — proposal and next steps

Hi Alice / Jared — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can put a scoped rate/quota proposal in front of procurement.

Recap of the workload we discussed (please correct if I mis-specified):
- Peak concurrent *streams* (bi-directional, chunked streaming): ~60 concurrent streaming sessions during peak.
- Non-streaming parallel requests (short text generation): ~300 RPS sustained, burstable to ~700 RPS within a 60s window.
- Typical prompt + response token length: 50–300 tokens (mode ~120).
- Latency SLOs: target p95 generation latency < 250 ms for short requests (<128 tokens); for streaming sessions we expect first-byte p95 < 200 ms and steady-state per-chunk p95 < 120 ms.
- Availability: multi-region failover (primary us-west, DR us-east) — want SLA language on regional fallback.

Open questions for BrightBank to confirm (needed to finalize rate/quota tiers):
1) Confirm session duration distribution (median / 95th pct) for streaming sessions.
2) Clarify how you count concurrency — by TCP connection, by JWT session, or by logical conversation?
3) Are you planning to multiplex multiple logical conversations over single connection (yes/no)?
4) Any hard procurement constraints around rate-limiting behavior (e.g. prefer 429 vs queued throttling)?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll draft a two-tier rate/quota proposal that covers (A) committed baseline with guaranteed concurrency and (B) burst buffer with controlled throttling/fallback.
- Ben (SE) will run a short sizing sim and produce bandwidth estimates for your real mix; we’ll attach that as a spreadsheet.
- If that looks good, we can spin up a 2-week canary in your US-W primary with monitoring dashboards and a fallback model variant to keep latency under SLO during spikes.

I’m attaching a short template outline of the connection/pool options we typically offer (connection-per-token, connection-per-session, multiplexing guidance). Ben and Monica are on copy to pull numbers.

Can you confirm the open questions above and whether procurement needs a formal rate table for contract redlines?

Thanks,
Michael

Thanks, Michael — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Session metrics: median streaming session length ~90s, 95th pct ~8 minutes (sessions are mostly short interactive lookups with occasional longer analyst sessions).
- Concurrency counting: we count by logical conversation token (JWT session). Each user may open multiple tabs but we only count active conversations. We do not plan to multiplex separate conversations over a single JWT.
- Multiplexing: NOT planned for our initial rollout — we expect one logical session = one connection.
- Preferred throttling behavior: procurement prefers deterministic rate limits and explicit 429 responses when a lease is exceeded; delayed queuing is a last resort.

Procurement note: procurement asked if you can provide a clear table of committed concurrency, burst allowance, and P95 latency commitments to include in the SOW. They also asked for a short description about how fallback model variants will be used when capacity is constrained.

If you can send the rate table + a brief paragraph about fallback behavior by Monday 22 Jun, we’ll circulate internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alice
Alice Chen

Hi Alice — thanks for the clarifications, that helps a lot. Tagging Ben and Monica to lock numbers and the SOW phrasing. Below is Redwood’s proposed starting table (we’ll attach a formal PDF for procurement):

Proposed rate/quota tiers (initial):
- Committed baseline:
  - Guaranteed concurrent sessions (JWT-counted): 60 guaranteed sessions
  - Sustained short-request throughput: 300 RPS (average tokens 120)
  - SLA target: p95 gen latency < 250 ms for short requests; streaming first-byte p95 < 200 ms
- Burst buffer (contracted burst window):
  - Burst allowance: +250% for up to 60 seconds (i.e., can hit ~750 RPS for short periods)
  - Additional concurrent sessions: allowed up to 150 concurrent sessions for a max 5-minute ramp with 429s after breach
- Fallback policy:
  - On capacity pressure, Redwood will automatically route to a smaller, lower-cost model variant for best-effort continuity (documented quality deltas in appendix). 429s emitted when active concurrent sessions exceed contracted burst+baseline and queue is full.

Monitoring & trial:
- Two-week canary: Redwood will instrument per-session traces, per-route latency histograms, and token-level cost dashboard.
- We will provide a CSV with bandwidth and expected egress for your network team.

Next actions (owner / ETA):
- Ben Carter (SE): produce bandwidth-estimates.csv and a one-page latency/throughput runbook — ETA: Mon 22 Jun.
- Monica Patel (CS): draft the SOW language for committed concurrency, burst behavior, and fallback model usage — ETA: Mon 22 Jun.
- Michael Grant: package formal rate table + PDF SOW and share with procurement — ETA: Tue 23 Jun.

I’ve attached a draft redwood-conn-proposal.pdf for procurement review. If that aligns, we can turn it into an addendum to the MSA and include the numeric table.

Thanks — talk soon.
Michael
